correctness.rationale: Conditional on risk r, the focal action saves expected endowment br only when exactly m-1 peers contribute; cost c is paid in every contributing state. Shared risk gives one switch in the hypergeometric pivotal probability, hence the two affine payoff differences. The pointwise positive rule is optimal uniquely a.e. because zeros are isolated (a zero-probability piece is the constant -c). Below tau, a positive-length cooperation segment exists iff alpha<tau; a positive-length gap after tau and a nonempty high segment require tau<gamma<1. A tie at gamma=tau is not a positive-measure gap. Each piece contributes at most one strict cooperation component. In the two-window regime the threshold value U(t)=integral_t^1 Delta(r) dr increases, decreases, increases and decreases across the three boundaries alpha, tau, gamma; the only maximizing candidates are alpha and gamma. Their gains are H+E_-−E_+ and H, with H the high positive area, E_- the low positive area and E_+ the absolute gap loss. The unrestricted gain is H+E_-, giving regret min(E_-, E_+). Independent exact enumeration of the 190 peer pairs found 100 and 36 pivotal pairs in the two regimes, alpha=3/10 and gamma=5/6, E_-=E_+=b/95 and H=b/380; the unrestricted and restricted gains are b/76 and b/380, and both cutoffs tie.
residual_risks: Uniform atomless shared risk, fixed composition, one synchronized cutoff, independent peer draw, and risk-only focal policies. The finite enumeration checks the witness, not the continuous optimization or an equilibrium claim.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Pointwise optimization is genuinely the same principle and is prior art, not hidden by different notation. Exchanging random quota for observed risk is not an equivalent model: the cutoff changes pivotality through synchronized actions, and risk also multiplies the benefit.

originality.rationale: Zhou et al. already supply the shared uniform risk setting and tolerance strategies; Fernández Domingos et al. already give pivotal marginal payoff and pointwise informed optimization in a different uncertain-quota problem. The defensible distinction is the exact boundary for two separated windows, optimal upper-tail regret and its attainable finite witness in the fixed-composition shared-risk setting. Neither the underlying game principles nor general nonmonotonicity are credited as new. A close same-day group-level result was compared on content.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies a sharp, feasible counterexample to treating threshold rules as a best-response class when a shared signal changes co-player actions. Its exact class-restriction loss and the finite tie with a factor-five gross decision gain show a genuine effect and give a quantitative test for a policy-space assumption used in the existing setting. The sign rule alone would not have this value.
residual_risks: No welfare, information-purchase, equilibrium, empirical behavior or evolutionary inference follows.
